title: Flatten nested totals into small named methods

blocks.text: Three levels of nested `stream().map(...reduce...)` inside one lambda are hard to read. The page's cure is a small method for each level, each pipeline calling the next one by name, with `mapToDouble(...).sum()` for the sums. That shape is advice; the tests check the totals.

The file declares `enum Status { PENDING, COMPLETED }`, `record Item(double price)`, `record Order(Status status, List<Item> items)` and `record Customer(String name, List<Order> orders)`. Write four static methods of `Totals`:

items: `double orderTotal(Order order)`: the sum of the order's item prices.
`double customerTotal(Customer customer)`: the sum of the customer's order totals.
`List<Double> customerTotals(List<Customer> customers)`: each customer's total, in order.
`double completedRevenue(List<Order> orders)`: the sum of item prices over `COMPLETED` orders only, counting only prices above zero.

blocks.text: An order can be empty and so can a customer's order list; `completedRevenue` has two filters, not one.

cases.says: Order, customer and completed-revenue totals add up the item prices.
An order with no items, or a customer with no orders, totals 0.0 rather than failing.
completedRevenue leaves out orders that are not COMPLETED.
completedRevenue skips item prices that are zero or below.

concepts: Totals over nested collections start from zero when a collection is empty, and each filter in the chain applies on its own.
